# Copilot Instructions

## Project Overview

This is a **component comparison tool** for analyzing and comparing UI components across multiple brand websites (currently FBTO and Centraal Beheer — two Dutch insurance brands). It extracts component usage data from Sitecore CMS analysis reports and provides:

1. A **Next.js web app** (`src/`) for browsing and comparing components across brands
2. An **offline analysis pipeline** (`scripts/`) that detects visually and functionally similar components across brands using perceptual hashing, name similarity, and DOM structural analysis
3. A **manual review system** that lets users mark pairs as confirmed-same or not-the-same, stored in `data/manual-review.json`

## Repository Structure

```
data/
  {brand}-report/
    extracted-data.json       # Component list: names, usage counts, page URLs
    component-selectors.json  # CSS selectors per component
    report.html               # Sitecore analysis report with embedded screenshots
    screenshots/              # Extracted PNG screenshots (generated by npm run analyze)
  similarity.json             # Cross-brand similarity scores (generated by npm run analyze)
  manual-review.json          # Manual review decisions — edited via the UI, persisted on server

scripts/
  analyze-similarity.ts       # Main analysis entry point — run with npm run analyze
  extract-screenshots.ts      # Extracts base64 screenshots from report.html
  similarity/
    name.ts                   # Token Jaccard name similarity with Dutch→English synonyms
    visual.ts                 # Perceptual hash (pHash) image similarity using sharp
    structural.ts             # DOM tag-sequence structural similarity

src/                          # Next.js app (App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS)
  app/
    page.tsx                  # Overview: stat cards + component comparison table with thumbnails
    components/[name]/
      page.tsx                # Detail page: brand panels + similar components grouped by review status
    api/review/
      route.ts                # GET/POST API for reading and writing manual-review.json
  components/
    ReviewButtons.tsx          # Client component — confirm/reject buttons with active state
    ReviewBadge.tsx            # Client component — inline read-only badge for overview table
    SimilarComponentsSection.tsx  # Client component — groups similar cards by review status
  lib/
    brands.ts                 # BRANDS registry — single source of truth for all brands
    types.ts                  # Shared TypeScript types
    data.ts                   # Data access: getAllBrandsData(), getSimilarPairs(), getScreenshotUrl(), buildPairKey()
  public/
    screenshots/
      {brand}/                # Screenshots served to the Next.js app (copied by analyze script)
```

## Development Commands

```bash
# From repo root — run similarity analysis (extract screenshots + compute scores)
npm run analyze

# From src/ — start the Next.js dev server
cd src && npm run dev         # → http://localhost:3000

# From src/ — production build
cd src && npm run build
```

## Adding a New Brand

1. Place report files in `data/{brand-id}-report/`:
   - `extracted-data.json`
   - `component-selectors.json`
   - `report.html` (with embedded screenshots)
2. Register the brand in `src/lib/brands.ts`:
   ```ts
   { id: 'new-brand', name: 'Display Name', dataDir: 'new-brand-report' }
   ```
3. Run `npm run analyze` from repo root
4. Rebuild/restart the Next.js app

## Architecture

- **Data layer**: All brand data is read from `data/` via Node.js `fs` in Next.js Server Components at build time (SSG). No API routes or client-side fetching needed — except the review API.
- **Similarity pipeline**: Runs offline (`npm run analyze`). Three signals — visual pHash (50%), name Jaccard with Dutch/English synonym normalization (30%), DOM structural tag-sequence (20%). Emits pairs scoring ≥ 0.4 into `data/similarity.json`.
- **Manual review**: `/api/review` is a dynamic Next.js Route Handler. GET returns `data/manual-review.json`; POST writes to it. The `SimilarComponentsSection` client component fetches reviews on mount and re-fetches after each save to re-sort cards live.
- **UI**: Pages are statically generated. Client components (`ReviewButtons`, `ReviewBadge`, `SimilarComponentsSection`) fetch review state from `/api/review` at runtime.
- **Screenshots**: Extracted from embedded base64 PNGs in `report.html`. Stored in `data/{brand}-report/screenshots/` and copied to `src/public/screenshots/{brand}/` for the web app.

## Manual Review System

The detail page groups similar components into three sections, re-ordered live after each review action:

1. **✓ Confirmed same** (green) — top
2. **? Needs review** (yellow) — middle (default for all new pairs)
3. **✕ Not the same** (red) — bottom

Review state is persisted in `data/manual-review.json`. The overview table shows a `ReviewBadge` for the best-match pair. Clicking an active button undoes the selection (returns to "unreviewed").

Pair keys follow the format: `{brandA}::{componentA}::{brandB}::{componentB}` — always in the stored order from `similarity.json`. Use `buildPairKey(pair)` from `data.ts` to generate them.

## Conventions

- Brand IDs are lowercase slugs (e.g., `fbto`, `cb`)
- Component names are used as-is from the source data (may be Dutch or English)
- `getScreenshotUrl()` returns `null` for components without screenshots — always handle the null case in UI
- `buildPairKey(pair)` in `src/lib/data.ts` produces canonical pair keys for review lookups
- The `BRANDS` array in `src/lib/brands.ts` is the single source of truth — do not hardcode brand IDs elsewhere
- Scripts use ESM (`"type": "module"` in root `package.json`) and run with `tsx`
- The Next.js app lives in `src/` with its own `package.json` — keep root and `src/` dependencies separate
- Do not add client-side event handlers (`onClick`, `onError`, etc.) to Next.js Server Components — use a `'use client'` wrapper
